value: Difference in activation for prayer versus other (news plus passive) was inversely correlated with self-reported ratings of alcohol craving in the prayer condition in the bilateral posterior cingulate gyrus, bilateral supramarginal gyrus, right-anterior middle prefrontal gyrus, and right medial frontal gyrus.

The inverse correlation could be interpreted to indicate that for participants who experienced prayer to reduce their perceived craving, the self-related aspects of experience did not need to be suppressed as much.

presentation_software.value: E-Prime 2.0 Professional; operating system not reported.

spans.text: The fMRI protocol with still images was designed using E-Prime 2.0 Professional

instructions.value: In the prayer condition, participants read the standard AA Step 3 prayer and the Serenity Prayer, adjusted for length, and kept the intent of the prayer in mind while viewing alcohol-related images. In the passive condition, they were instructed to view the stimuli passively and allow their reactions without attempting to suppress them. In the news condition, they read unrelated information and kept its content in mind. After each image, they rated craving from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much).

stimuli.value: Ninety still photographs of alcohol-craving-inducing images, including images selected from the Normative Appetitive Picture System and supplemental alcohol-related images from the web; 30 images per condition.

spans.text: In total 90 images were used (30 per condition).

value: In-scanner alcohol-craving ratings after each image on a 5-point scale (1=not at all, 5=very much)
